findings.claim: _reply_problem calls cx.parse_reply(rd.replay(entry)), but rd.replay already delegates to parse() and returns a parsed dict (or None). cx.parse_reply converts a dict argument via str(raw) into Python single-quoted dict syntax, failing JSON decoding and returning None. Thus every valid reader and adjudicator reply is judged 'unreadable reply: {who}', causing item_verdict to quarantine 100% of assessed trials into QUARANTINE.json and leaving served output objects completely empty.
findings.guidance_basis: Handbook 8.2 and RoB 2 serving specification (PROMPT.txt / RESPONSES.md r28-r29): valid dual readings and adjudications must be preserved and written to served trial objects (outputs/robgrade/served/rob2/<slug>.json); only genuinely malformed or conflicting replies may be quarantined.
findings.failing_test: entry with valid reply where rd.replay(entry) returns parsed dict {'answers': [{'qid': '1.2', 'answer': 'PY'}]} -> _reply_problem(entry, 'codex') returns 'unreadable reply: codex' instead of None.

findings.claim: Test helper _world mocks sv.rd.replay as returning bytes ((replies.get(...) or '').encode()) instead of the parsed dict returned by real rd.replay (which calls parse()). This contract violation masked the double-parsing defect in _reply_problem, allowing test_PLANT_r29_a_clean_item_passes to pass spuriously while real execution quarantines all trials.
findings.guidance_basis: AGENTS.md test integrity and fail-closed requirements: test fixtures must obey the type contracts of mocked pipeline functions. Mocking bytes instead of dict masks catastrophic failure in item_verdict.
findings.failing_test: _world with sv.rd.replay returning json.loads(GOOD) (conforming to real rd.replay's dict contract) -> test_PLANT_r29_a_clean_item_passes fails with assert 'unreadable reply: codex' is None.
